quotes.text: Serverless doesn't mean no servers. It means you don't think about them. And that distinction changes everything about how you build software.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the most common misconception about serverless in one line.

quotes.text: The combination of triggers and bindings is what makes Azure Functions so powerful that you write the business logic, the actual decision making code, the platform handles all the integration.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core programming model of Azure Functions.

quotes.text: Ask yourself whether the task is short, whether it's event-driven and whether it's stateless. If you answered yes to all three, Azure Functions is probably the right tool.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple three-question test for choosing Azure Functions.

quotes.text: Here's a simple rule of thumb. If you can describe the job in one sentence, it's probably a good candidate for a function.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable heuristic for scoping serverless workloads.

quotes.text: The golden rule for all of this is to keep your functions small, focused, and stateless. One job per function. Nothing more.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's best practices into one rule.

takeaways: Serverless does not mean no servers: Azure Functions runs small, stateless pieces of code in response to events while the platform handles servers, patching and scaling.
Every function has exactly one trigger, and optional input and output bindings connect it to storage, queues and databases without SDK boilerplate.
Start with the Consumption plan and its free grant, but watch timeouts, cold starts and authentication, and enable Application Insights from day one.
hook: Serverless is one of the most misunderstood terms in cloud computing. This episode explains Azure Functions in plain English for developers and IT pros who want to run code without managing servers. You learn how triggers, bindings and the Consumption plan work, when functions fit, and which beginner mistakes to avoid.
